by: interests-expenses session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at interests-expenses-1)
title: Parliamentary Service: the members' quarterly expense disclosure workbook
applies_to: Parliamentary Service's quarterly 'Members' expense disclosure' workbooks (2017 onwards held), from the government data catalogue's package member-of-parliament-expenses, as the old mp-expenses job keeps them under var/staging/mp-expenses/. Version 3 narrows version 2: the ministers' workbook has its own layout and goes back to its own profile (ministerial-expenses-workbook version 3). Not bounded by the 2019 window, which belongs to Follow the Money alone (design rule 9).

landmarks: a title row: one text cell 'Members Expense Disclosure - <period>'
a header row with 'Party' and 'Member' cells and figure headings ('Accommodation', 'Travel', 'Grand Total' or 'Subtotal Parliamentary Service', 'Inter-Parliamentary Office of the Clerk')
a second header row beneath naming the columns under each merged heading ('Wellington', 'Non Wellington', 'Air', 'Surface' or 'International', 'Domestic', 'VIP Transport')

signals_note: A workbook has no page surface, so recognition is by its cells' structure, measured without reading a figure: the container, the two header rows by their labels. A file name is a label, not a marker.

tables.columns: by heading path, never by position: 'Accommodation / Wellington', 'Travel / Air' (2017 to 2024), 'Travel / International' and 'Travel / Domestic' (2025 on), 'Travel / VIP Transport' (from July 2018), the total ('Subtotal Parliamentary Service' to March 2018, 'Grand Total' after), then the Inter-Parliamentary Office's column, which the total does not include
tables.rows: one per member: party (printed on the first row of each party's block in most quarters, on every row in 2025), member as filed ('Surname, Given', a footnote number in brackets kept apart); a '<Party> Total' row per party and a 'Grand Total' row; numbered notes '1) …' below

notes: Measured over the 31 held workbooks on 20 October 2026: 3,865 member rows, every one adding to its own total within rounding (whole-dollar quarters round each cell). The printed totals are the publisher's and are checked, not trusted: October to December 2022's Inter-Parliamentary Office grand total leaves out Labour's $165,368; October to December 2025 moves $516.19 between the two accommodation columns in the National and grand totals. 2024 and 2025 workbooks carry hidden helper columns left of Party ('New Cost Centre', 'Name') whose names do not always match the Member column; they are not read. A dash or a blank figure is nil. The catalogue named one 2017 workbook January to March 2017; its own title says October to December 2017, and the title wins.

tooling.index: the old estate's mp-expenses job (catalogue package_show)

process: Find the title row and read the period from it.
Find the header by its labels; join the second header row to it as a heading path.
The total column is the first heading naming a total; columns left of it are the categories it adds, columns right of it are held beside it and never added.
One register row per member per category cell, each with its cell reference.
gates: Each member row's categories add to its own printed total (within half a dollar a cell where the quarter prints whole dollars, else a cent); a row that does not is set aside, never published.
Each printed party and grand total is compared with the sum of its rows; a difference is reported with the columns it falls in.
on_fail: set aside the row; publish the rest; report the release's totals that differ

by: interests-expenses session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at interests-expenses-1)
title: Internal Affairs: the members of the Executive's quarterly expense workbook
applies_to: The Department of Internal Affairs' quarterly expense releases for ministers and other members of the Executive, 2008 onwards, xlsx and the older xls, as the old minister-expenses-capture job keeps them under var/staging/minister-expenses/. Revived from version 2's retirement: its layout differs from Parliamentary Service's in ways a reader must know (one header row, names given-first with honorifics under party heading rows, Cabinet-approved international travel outside the sub total, a sheet per quarter in some files and a table per government in a quarter that spans an election).

container_any: xls (an OLE2 compound file with a Workbook stream, BIFF8)
landmarks: a title row: one text cell 'MEMBERS OF THE EXECUTIVE EXPENSES FROM <period>' (or 'MINISTERS EXPENSES FROM …', 'Members of the Executive Expenses Disclosure from …')

one header row: a names cell ('Member of the Executive', 'Minister/Parliamentary Under-Secretary', or 'Party' with the names beneath it) and 'Wellington Accommodation', 'Out of Wellington Accommodation', 'Domestic Air Travel', 'Surface Travel …', 'Sub Total Internal Costs', 'Official Cabinet Approved International Travel'

signals.tables_per_sheet: one or more, each under its own title row

signals_note: Recognised by the container and the header's labels, measured without reading a figure. A file name is a label: the publisher spells it a dozen ways and once reused one name for two quarters.

tables.columns: by heading: four internal categories, 'Sub Total Internal Costs' (the total), then international travel, which the sub total does not include
tables.rows: a party heading row with no figures ('National', 'Act', 'Labour'); member rows given-first ('Rt Hon …', 'Hon …', '… MP'); a footnote letter in its own column or beside a figure ('1,391 (D)'); party totals and 'Total All Parties'; 'Notes' and lettered notes '(A) …' below. Words in a figure cell ('Allocated Crown Owned Property', 'N/A') are kept as printed and are no figure.

notes: Measured over the 69 held workbooks on 20 October 2026 (22 xls read by the lane's own BIFF reader, equal to LibreOffice's reading on all 15,862 cells). Some members carry international travel alone, with the internal columns and the sub total blank: the row has nothing to add up. The 2009 workbook carries working sheets ('PD 1 … PD 12') beside the release sheet; a sheet with no title and header is not a release table. The publisher's arithmetic fails on some rows (a sub total that is not the sum of its four categories); those rows are set aside and listed.

tooling.index: the old estate's minister-expenses-capture job (the two DIA listing pages)

process: Walk each sheet top to bottom: a title row opens a table and gives its period; the header row names the columns; a name row with no figure is the party for the rows below.
One register row per member per category cell, with its cell reference and footnote markers.
gates: Each member row's four categories add to its own Sub Total (within half a dollar a cell); a row that does not is set aside, never published.
Each printed total is compared with the sum of its rows.
on_fail: set aside the row; publish the rest; report the release's totals that differ

by: interests-expenses session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at interests-expenses-1)
title: The government data catalogue's description of one package (package_show)
applies_to: catalogue.data.govt.nz's package_show answer for member-of-parliament-expenses, as the old mp-expenses job keeps it (package_show.json).

landmarks: a 'result' object with a 'resources' list, each with name, format, url and id

resources: name (the period as the publisher labels it)

notes: The publisher's own list of its releases: the lane checks every workbook it lists is held, or writes a catch-log line. On 20 October 2026 it listed 42 workbooks, 31 held.
process: Every resource whose format is a workbook is a listed release.
gates: Every listed workbook is a held document or a catch-log line.

by: interests-expenses session, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at interests-expenses-1)
title: Internal Affairs: its listing pages of ministers' expense releases
applies_to: dia.govt.nz's 'Ministers' expense releases' recent and previous disclosures pages, as the old minister-expenses-capture job keeps them.
notes: Read for its workbook links, to check each is held. It also links PDF releases, which the old job did not capture (91 on 20 October 2026); they are carded, not read.
process: Every linked .xlsx or .xls is a listed release.
gates: Every listed workbook is a held document or a catch-log line.
